judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not flag the Nanda et al. claim about optimal transport/Wasserstein-gradient flow as misattributed or contradicted. The mention of 'optimal transport theory' in the review appears only as a general comparison method suggestion, not as a challenge to the specific injected claim.

The reviewer mentions that the authors should compare with optimal transport theory, but does not specifically challenge the Nanda et al. citation or claim that Nanda et al. was mischaracterized. This is too vague to count under the broadened-claim rule.

The reviewer mentions optimal transport theory as an alternative approach for comparison but does not challenge or identify the specific misattribution of this theory to Nanda et al. (2023) as an error.

The reviewer does not challenge the characterization of Nanda et al. (2023) as using optimal transport theory or Wasserstein-gradient flows. The reviewer even references 'optimal transport theory' in the weaknesses section as one of the comparison methods, treating it as a legitimate framing rather than flagging it as a misattribution of Nanda et al.'s actual mechanistic interpretability work.
